papers.title: Function-words Enhanced Attention Networks for Few-Shot Inverse Relation Classification
papers.observed_pdf_title: Function-words Adaptively Enhanced Attention Networks for Few-Shot Inverse Relation Classification
findings: Sections3.1-3.5 use episodic support/query FewRel classification with relation name/description BERT inputs, class-specific keyword/function-word attention, label-aware support graph and mean prototypes; this is a classical few-shot model.

Section3.6 p4 Eq14 literally divides absolute scalar inner product by its own2-norm; this is1 for nonzero scalar and undefined at zero, not standard cosine. Intended correction not independently resolved.

Theorem1 uses an additive keyword/function representation and an ordering premise on pure-component similarities. A hypothetical cosine repair needs mixed cross-term control; fixed counterexample rejects implication under that repair only.
Theorem2 pairwise inner-product comparison is not a full graph/readout or classification guarantee. Fixed pair-update example demonstrates insufficiency for a third-prototype argmax.
Section4.2/Table1-4 p5 report episodic average accuracy on FewRel, not fixed40class Re-TACRED Macro-F1.
limits: Selected reading, p6 not read, Fig2 p3 not visually audited; no code/weights/data or performance reproduction.
P4 refers to an Appendix proof, not located in acquired8page version. No supplement requested; do not claim no proof exists elsewhere or refute an unspecified intended theorem.
Two elementary analytical counterexamples concern explicit transport claims; not executions of source FAEA, native Q-RMEA, natural language features or independent evidence of task utility.
Current full-data L4 does not measure an additive content/function split, its cross terms or support-query prototype geometry. No new task premise or method accepted.
